# Agatha Sowerby

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mrs. Agatha  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P15](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0015), [v1 c9 P21](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0021)</sub>; Mrs. Sowerby  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P2](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

She is described as heavy and awkward in build. She is often seen sitting by her kitchen window working on quilts with her knitting needles.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P19](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0019), [v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000)_

## Personality

Agatha Sowerby is an outspoken, sharp-tongued, and opinionated woman who takes pride in expressing her thoughts without fear or partiality. Often viewed as an inveterate meddler who compresses whole sermons into a few blunt words, she nevertheless possesses a deeply compassionate heart and quietly aids those in need. She firmly believes in strict discipline and physical correction for misbehaving children.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P3](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0003), [v2 c9 P10](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0010), [v2 c10 P90](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0090)_

## History

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby visited Grey Shutters shortly after Obed Abernethy brought the young orphan Nell home. During the visit, she insulted Nell's plain appearance and bright red hair, triggering a furious outburst from the girl. While shocked by Nell's temper, Agatha advised Thirza Abernethy to use a birch rod to discipline her. Years later, she actively solicited contributions for local projects, such as asking Mr. Pettifer for money to purchase a vestry room carpet. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she faithfully cared for him in their home while continuing her community involvement.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P15](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0015), [v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c9 P21](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0021), [v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), [v2 c8 P0](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0000), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c22 P11](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0011), [v2 c22 P13](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0013)_
